title: Bruke det i væresetninger — using det in weather sentences
goal: Use fixed det when weather or ambient predication has no semantic subject.

objectives.statement: Use fixed det when weather or ambient predication has no semantic subject.

spans.value: Mina and Jonas are preparing to meet outside a café in Bergen. Mina is already on her way, but the weather is getting worse.
Hei, Jonas. Er du på vei?

spans.value: Ikke ennå. Hvordan er været der?

spans.value: Det regner, og det blåser ganske mye.

blocks.translation: It’s raining, and it’s quite windy.

spans.value: Å nei. Er det kaldt også?

blocks.translation: Oh no. Is it cold too?

spans.value: Ja, det er kaldt, og det begynner å bli mørkt.

spans.value: Da møtes vi inne på kafeen.

blocks.translation: Then we’ll meet inside the café.

spans.value: God idé. Det er varmt og hyggelig der inne.

blocks.translation: Good idea. It’s warm and pleasant inside.

when weather or an ambient condition has no real person or thing performing the action or possessing the quality.
English also commonly uses “it” in weather expressions:
in much the same way. This use is often called a dummy subject or formal subject. You do not need to analyze that label when speaking. The practical point is simple:

spans.value: The important choice is not whether English happens to include the word “it” in every translation. The important choice is whether Norwegian needs a subject even though no particular person or thing is being described.

sections.title: Transfer: a morning at the cabin

spans.value: The next weekend, Jonas is staying at a cabin. Mina asks whether they can go for a walk. Conditions are different from the café scene: it is snowing, the cabin is warm, and daylight is beginning to fade.

prompt.value: Choose the interpretation that correctly covers Mina's weather and ambient statements in the café call. What does repeated «det» do, and what conditions do the statements report?

options.text: In each sentence, «det» names the weather or another object that is raining, windy, cold, dark, warm, or pleasant.
options.why: In these statements, «det» does not refer to a named object.

options.text: Only «det regner» and «det blåser ganske mye» use fixed «det». In the other sentences, «det» refers to a particular cold, dark, warm, or pleasant thing.
options.why: The ambient sentences with «det er» and «det begynner å bli» also use fixed «det» without a named semantic subject.

options.text: «Det regner» (It's raining), «det blåser ganske mye» (It's quite windy), «det er kaldt» (It's cold), «det begynner å bli mørkt» (It's starting to get dark), and «det er varmt og hyggelig der inne» (It's warm and pleasant inside) all use fixed «det» as the grammatical subject. «Det» does not name an object.
options.why: Norwegian uses fixed «det» when no person or thing is the semantic subject; the sentences report the listed weather and ambient conditions.

prompt.value: Complete the three Norwegian reports. The meanings are rain in Bergen today, snow in Oslo today, and wind by the sea today, in that order. Select the full weather expression; keep «det» and do not put «er» before the weather verb.

explanation.value: Weather and ambient clauses use fixed «det». Weather verbs are direct («det regner»), while adjective conditions use neuter singular after «er/blir» («det er varmt», «det blir mørkt»).

prompt.value: Classify each Norwegian sentence by what it describes: a named thing as subject, or a general ambient condition with fixed «det». Judge only whether the sentence has a named semantic subject; adjective agreement is not the focus.

buckets.label: Named subject: a particular thing is described.
Ambient condition: no named semantic subject; fixed «det» is used.

items.text: Kaffen er kald. — The coffee is cold.
Rommet er mørkt. — The room is dark.
Ovnen er varm. — The oven is hot.

prompt.value: Build the complete Norwegian sentence meaning “It is warm and pleasant inside.” Use every supplied token exactly once.
Complete two Norwegian observations. Use «er» for the current condition and «blir» for the developing condition. Keep fixed «det» in both meanings.

Answer these three questions in Norwegian. Write one complete weather or ambient statement for each. Include the requested place or time information, and use rain for the first answer, cold for the second, and wind for the third. Include Bergen and i dag in the first answer, hytta and om morgenen in the second, and sjøen and i dag in the third. 1. «Hvordan er været i Bergen i dag?» — What is the weather like in Bergen today? 2. «Hvordan er det på hytta om morgenen?» — What is it like at the cabin in the morning? 3. «Hvordan er det ved sjøen i dag?» — What is it like by the sea today?

payload.judge_prompt: Check the three answers separately and report evidence for every required weather, place, time, and fixed-«det» criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants when the requested numbered answer remains clear.

prompt.value: You are at a mountain cabin before deciding whether to go for a walk. Write a short connected report in Norwegian with four complete statements: report snow outside, cold outdoors, warmth inside, and darkness that is increasing. Use fixed «det» in every weather or ambient statement because no particular person or thing is the semantic subject. Use your own natural Bokmål wording and do not copy a lesson sentence verbatim.
